name: cargo-mutants
desc: Inject bugs and see if your tests catch them
why: Injects bugs into Rust code to see which tests catch them; a clever inversion of testing, though aimed at developers.

brief.what_it_is: cargo-mutants is a mutation testing tool for Rust. It takes a Rust source tree and automatically makes small changes to the code (mutants) that act like inserted bugs, then runs the tests against each one. Its output is a report of which bugs the tests failed to catch, which points to places where the tests may be insufficient. It is run as a Cargo subcommand, `cargo mutants`, and can be restricted to a single file.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a gap in coverage measurement: coverage 'tell[s] you what code is reached by a test, and not whether the test really checks anything about the behavior of the code.' Mutation testing is offered as the different information: whether the tests actually check the code's behavior.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not describe the internals in detail. It says the tool finds 'places where bugs could be inserted without causing any tests to fail,' and that it works on trees whose non-flaky tests run under `cargo test` or `cargo nextest run`. The author's design notes (DESIGN.md) and the user guide at mutants.rs were linked but not fetched.

commands_seen.context: Installs the tool from crates.io, the README's primary install method.
Quick start: run from inside a Rust source directory to generate and test mutants.
Generates mutants in only one file, src/something.rs.

brief.install_notes: Primary install is `cargo install --locked cargo-mutants`, which needs a Rust toolchain. The README also mentions cargo-binstall and prebuilt binaries on GitHub releases as alternatives. The tree needs non-flaky tests that run under `cargo test` or `cargo nextest run`. The README points to a CI integration guide at mutants.rs/ci.html for incremental testing of pull requests. No accounts or extra configuration are mentioned.
brief.standout: It inverts the usual testing question. Instead of asking whether the code is covered, it deliberately breaks the code and asks whether any test notices. The README says the goal is to be easy to run on any Rust tree and to tell you something interesting, not just to produce a number.
brief.status: Maintained, though part-time. The README's project status section says it is a 'semi-actively-maintained spare time project,' with less recent time for the author, PRs and bugs read with higher latency, and releases expected 'every few months at worst.' The README date reads 'As of August 2026.' I did not check the release page or commit history, so no exact last-release date is confirmed.
brief.caveats: Only Rust, and only trees with non-flaky tests under cargo test or cargo nextest. The README says it is provided 'as-is with no warranty of any kind.' The author describes it as 'very usable as it is' but says there is room for more mutation types. The README does not discuss licensing terms in the parts I read. The author's wording invites feedback on false positives, so expect some noise.
quotes: cargo-mutants helps you improve your program's quality by finding places where bugs could be inserted without causing any tests to fail.
Coverage measurements can be helpful, but they really tell you what code is _reached_ by a test, and not whether the test really _checks_ anything about the behavior of the code.
This software is provided as-is with no warranty of any kind.
